event.title: <show-title>A Bay of Blood</show-title>
event.headline: See Mario Bava invent modern the slasher.
event.description:
New 4K restoration by Severin Films.

After establishing the giallo genre with BLOOD AND BLACK LACE in 1964, Mario Bava revolutionized the horror landscape again with A BAY OF BLOOD. Set at a lakeside cabin, this primal scream of a film doesn’t merely hint at what’s to come with THE TEXAS CHAIN SAW MASSACRE and HALLOWEEN. Rather, it bursts onto the scene as the first slasher—fully formed, and without the threadbare hallmarks of the "proto" prefix. A BAY OF BLOOD delivers the goods in the slasher thrills department, and was the source material for two of the greatest kills in FRIDAY THE 13TH PART 2. Whether you’re a first-time or repeat viewer of A BAY OF BLOOD, you owe it to yourself to luxuriate in this newly-restored masterpiece of Italian horror.

show.headline: Chucky gets lucky in this camp horror classic

event.title: <show-title>Bride of Chucky</show-title>
event.description: Ten years after the events in CHILD’S PLAY 3, pint-size psychopath Chucky is resurrected in the name of love by his girlfriend Tiffany (Jennifer Tilly). But it’ll take a cross-country death-trip with a group of high school outcasts to really bring them together. The CHILD’S PLAY franchise is the only studio-backed horror series in history to be created and driven by an openly gay filmmaker. With BRIDE, creator-writer Don Mancini and director Ronny Yu deliver a joyful combination of outstanding gore, evil gags, gay-positive characterizations, and John Ritter as a crooked cop. But this movie’s secret weapon is Tilly, whose confident, take-no-shit performance made her an icon of 1990s horror. (Joseph A. Ziemba)

show.title: Little Shop of Horrors (1986)
show.headline: The iconic black comedy horror musical – back on the big screen

event.title: <show-title>Little Shop of Horrors (1986)</show-title>
event.headline: Oz, Ashman, and Menken’s iconically queer monster movie musical turns 40!
event.description:
Feed me, Seymour. Feed me all night long.

Alarm goes off at seven, and you start uptown. You put in your eight hours for the powers that have always been. Ugh, ain’t that the truth, Chiffon?

It’s been a hot minute since we’ve screened a musical for Queer Film Theory 101, so in honor of its 40th anniversary, we’re showing the melodic and incendiary critique of hustle culture, LITTLE SHOP OF HORRORS, from powerhouse writing duo Howard Ashman and Alan Menken and director Frank Oz. Well ahead of its time, this film tackles hot topics like urban decay, abusive dentistry, aggressively sexual plants, and presages the rise of influencer culture.

When dopey orphan-turned-beleaguered florist’s assistant Seymour (Rick Moranis) stumbles upon an exceptionally strange and exotic plant, he suddenly sees a way out of Skid Row for himself and the equally troubled object of his affection, Audrey (Ellen Green). Unfortunately for everyone involved, Seymour’s leafy meal ticket, Audrey II (Levi Stubbs), harbors murderous desires of its own, revealing itself as an extraterrestrial invader hell-bent on human domination.

Featuring an all-star cast including Steve Martin, John Candy, Tisha Campbell, and Bill Murray, unforgettable songs from Ashman and Menken, and incredible puppetry from Lyle Conway (THE DARK CRYSTAL, The Muppet Show), LITTLE SHOP OF HORRORS is perhaps the perfect movie musical. Don’t argue with us. Deeply queer, filled with critiques of capitalism, and catchy as hell, we can’t wait to celebrate this iconic musical's 40th anniversary with y’all as part of Queer Film Theory 101. And just a gentle reminder: don’t feed the plants!

show.title: The Birdcage
show.headline: Robin Williams and Nathan Lane try to play it straight

event.title: <show-title>The Birdcage</show-title>
event.headline: Williams & Lane burst open THE BIRDCAGE in this flamboyant farcical adaptation
event.description:
"My mother always said, 'Live on Fisher Island, get buried in Palm Beach. That way, you'll have the best of Florida.'"

Progress is not a straight line. I mean, I’m not sure it’s a line at all. It seems far more abstract and subjective. Like, listen: in 1996, when THE BIRDCAGE was first released, the idea of a mainstream comedy film with two gay leads (and many more openly queer characters) was controversial. I guess, unfortunately…it still is.

Based on the French farce film LA CAGE AUX FOLLES from 1978, Mike Nichols and Elaine May’s adaptation shifts the action from a drag club in the French Riviera to a drag club in South Beach, Florida…the American Riviera. When Armand Goldman (Robin Williams) learns that his son Val (Dan Futterman) is engaged to the daughter of conservative couple Senator Kevin Keeley (Gene Hackman) and Louise Keeley (Dianne Wiest), he’s put into an impossible situation. Pushed by Val to “straighten” out his life in preparation for meeting his fiancée Barbara’s (Calista Flockhart) parents, Armand struggles to manage his life partner Albert (Nathan Lane) with some dubious assistance from their housemaid Agador (Hank Azaria) and Val’s birth mother Katharine (Christine Brianski). Shenanigans ensue: there’s drag, Fosse, pierced toast, beckoning schmecken, and of course DRAG! WHEW! Grounded by hilarious and deeply heartfelt performances from Williams and Lane, THE BIRDCAGE is an incredible (if sometimes problematic) comedy helmed by the iconic duo of Nichols and May. Immensely quotable and uncomfortably relevant 30 years after its release, THE BIRDCAGE is a classic, and we’re so excited to screen it as part of Queer Film Theory 101!

event.title: <show-title>The Nutty Professor (1996)</show-title> <event-type-title>30th Anniversary</event-type-title>
event.headline: Eddie Murphy goes big in a tour de force comic performance
event.description:
It's hard to top how much of a one-man band Jerry Lewis was in his prime. With the original version of THE NUTTY PROFESSOR alone, he served as writer, director, producer, hero, and villain. But superstar Eddie Murphy is no slouch, and with this remake, he managed to one-up a comedy icon and revitalize his own career in the process.

In an incredible feat of acting and special effects, Murphy plays seven characters in this hilarious story of an overweight professor who magically loses 250 pounds but gains an obnoxious alter ego in the process. His performances are so jaw-droppingly funny, you'll be shouting, "Hercules! Hercules! Hercules!"

show.title: eXistenZ
show.headline: David Cronenberg's video game odyssey

event.title: <show-title>eXistenZ</show-title>
event.headline: Cronenberg's augmented reality video game head trip!
event.description: Lubricate your bioport and prepare to jack in to David Cronenberg's twisty thriller set in a near-future world of ultra-realistic video games, corporate espionage, and guns made from bones and teeth. Fleshy game systems connect directly to players' spinal columns via an umbilical-cord-like cable in Cronenberg's mutant vision of video game culture. Part Hitchcock's 39 STEPS, part VIDEODROME, EXISTENZ is pure Cronenberg paranoia, sex panic, and body horror. Add in a dash of existential crisis, and you have yourself one of the great sci-fi masterpieces of 1999.

event.headline: Paired with the TV episode that inspired the film, "Space Seed"
event.description:
About STAR TREK II: THE WRATH OF KHAN
1982 | 113 mins.

It is 1980. Disappointed with the performance of the decidedly un-STAR WARS-like results of STAR TREK: THE MOTION PICTURE, Paramount executives approach television producer Harve Bennett about taking over the next outing of the Starship Enterprise...but for a far lower budget than the prior film and its special effects extravaganza.

To familiarize himself with the series, Bennett watched all 79 episodes of the original series, with one story – season one's "Space Seed" – igniting his imagination. The tale of an antiheroic superhuman named Khan who attempts to take over the Enterprise and who is left with his followers on an Earth-like planet to create their own utopia... well, it begged for a follow-up. Alongside co-writer Jack B. Sowards and young director Nicholas Meyer, Bennett created that follow-up, and set the stage for two more films that, though planned one-by-one, work as a perfect trilogy.

An epic revenge tale that also manages to pack in meditations on aging, regret, and how we deal with death, it’s the finest moment in the entire original series canon, and (arguably) one of the greatest science-fiction films ever made.

About "Space Seed" (S1E22)
1967 | 50 mins.

While on patrol in deep space, Captain Kirk and his crew find and revive a genetically engineered world conqueror and his compatriots from Earth's twentieth century.

event.description:
About STAR TREK IV: THE VOYAGE HOME
1989 | 119 mins.

The most acclaimed Star Trek adventure of all time with an important message. It’s the 23rd century, and a mysterious alien probe is threatening Earth by evaporating the oceans and destroying the atmosphere. In their frantic attempt to save mankind, Admiral Kirk and his crew must time-travel back to 1986 San Francisco, where they find a world of punk, pizza, and exact-change buses that are as alien to them as anything they have ever encountered in the far-off reaches of the galaxy. William Shatner and Leonard Nimoy return as Kirk and Spock, along with the entire Enterprise crew.

About "The City on the Edge of Forever" (S1E28)
1967 | 50 mins.

When a temporarily insane Dr. McCoy accidentally changes history and destroys his time, Kirk and Spock follow him to prevent the disaster, but the price to do so is high.

event.description:
About STAR TREK: THE MOTION PICTURE – DIRECTOR'S EDITION
1979 | 136 mins.

A decade after its cancelation from NBC, Star Trek made its triumphant return into popular culture with STAR TREK: THE MOTION PICTURE, a bold and expansive vision of the future fit for the silver screen.

Years after a promotion to Starfleet Command, Admiral Kirk re-takes the captain's chair of the newly-refit U.S.S. Enterprise after a deadly probe of unknown origin sets its course for Earth. Kirk's crew reunion is short-lived as he immediately clashes with his executive officer, the brash Decker, and contends with his former science officer Spock's mysterious and guarded return.

While still a mammoth technical achievement in 1979, Robert Wise's full directorial vision was restored in 2001 in the original Director's Edition. This 2022 version showcases its analog wizardry while also further integrating digital effects work, delivering the most comprehensive version to date.

About "The Changeling" (S2E3)
1967 | 50 mins.

A powerful artificially intelligent Earth probe, with a murderously twisted imperative, comes aboard the Enterprise and mistakes Captain Kirk for its creator.

marketStrings.value: The personal closed captioning device displays feature film dialogue and other audio in the form of English-language text for individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing.

The descriptive audio headset provides individuals who are blind or have low vision with an English-language narration of the details of the feature presentation that can't be understood by the soundtrack alone.

Upon request at the box office, we provide assistive listening headsets with amplified audio for those individuals who are hard of hearing. For guests who prefer to use their own hearing aids, neck loops, or cochlear implants, our assistive listening headsets have a 3.5mm headphone jack to connect to those devices.

In order to ensure the highest quality experience for all guests, you may not enter a movie after it has started. We’d love to see you up to 30 minutes early. Running late? No worries, we will happily exchange your ticket for a different showtime or a raincheck to a future show.

sessionAttributes.name: Infinity Vision
sessionAttributes.description: Infinity Vision is Disney's rigorous Premium Large Format certification, guaranteeing you an exceptional film presentation. Screens must be at least 45 feet wide, outfitted with Immersive sound like Dolby Atmos or 7.1, and brightness levels should reach either 14 footlamberts in 2D and/or 6 footlamberts in 3D.
